note: Two shipped plugins told the reader there was no built-in logger at all. The redaction assertions here are the security-relevant ones: they pin which direction the allow/deny lists point, and they pin the fact that a JSON body is not redacted — the claim most likely to be softened by accident.

assertions.claim: LogRequestHeaders defaults to false — the declaration ends at the closing brace with no initializer. Matching to end-of-line matters: `\s*(?!=)` backtracks to zero-width and passes even when the property gains `= true;`.
BodySizeLimit defaults to 32 KB — bodies are truncated, not dropped.
Only application/json and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies are ever logged.
The default RedactedKeys list is exactly the eleven keys the skill quotes.
RedactedHeaders is empty by default — header safety comes from the allow-list, not from this list.
A header is masked UNLESS it is on the known-safe allow-list — the safe direction. Authorization is not on that list.
Authorization is absent from KnownSafe.Headers, so it is masked.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, 'Authorization is not on that list'

assertions.claim: Query values are masked unless the key is known-safe (maskUnknownKeys: true).
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging and § Verify on the wire, checklist item 4

assertions.claim: A form body is masked by DENY-list only — a key not in RedactedKeys (card_number, cvv) prints in the clear, unlike the same key in a query string.
A non-form (i.e. JSON) body is logged VERBATIM, only truncated. This is the security-relevant claim in the whole logging section.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, 'does not redact a JSON body'

assertions.claim: The known-safe query keys are exactly the nine the skill lists.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Verify on the wire, checklist item 4

assertions.claim: The request line is emitted at Information and is on by default.
The request body is emitted at Trace.
Retry notices are emitted at Warning.
Every event is ANDed with the ILogger's own IsEnabled, and a per-call LogLevel REPLACES the per-switch default in both directions.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, the table preamble and the per-call override bullets

assertions.claim: The environment variable is consulted only when LoggerFactory is still null — so it is inert on the DI path.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, the three-state table and the env-var warning

assertions.claim: The variable is the client type name upper-cased plus _LOG.
The catch-all branch (trace) forces LogRequestBody on — unredacted JSON bodies to stderr, switched on from outside the code.
The built-in console logger writes to stderr.
